subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Washington Irving and the American Short Story
description: A micro-lesson that makes Washington Irving and the American Short Story usable.

hook.text: Washington Irving created the first famous American short stories, including a man who slept for twenty years.

buildup.text: Rip Van Winkle and The Legend of Sleepy Hollow established American fiction as distinct from British tradition.

discovery.text: Irving adapted German folktales and transplanted them into the Hudson Valley, creating an American mythology.

twist.text: He wrote these stories while living in England, homesick, proving that distance can sharpen national identity.

climax.text: Irving proved that a new nation could create its own literary tradition by reinventing borrowed legends.

punchline.text: American fiction was born from a homesick writer in England.

quiz.question: Where was Washington Irving when he wrote his famous American stories?
options: In the Hudson Valley of New York
On a ship crossing the Atlantic
